title: Three Ways Recorder
description: Write one real measure three ways, put a group's measures in order, add a group's weights, and measure the water a group drinks with a measuring jug.
modes: none. One flow, one phase at a time. The host mounts a phase (phase prop). With navigableDots true, or no phase, the child may jump phases with the dots (user mode); otherwise the dots show progress and the teacher agent drives window.toolApi (AI mode). The last phase, and a whole lesson, end on the summary page, where Free play and Play again sit. With navDots the dots are controls in AI mode too: a tap on a dot starts that phase.

stage.sizing: the frame is min(100vw, 177.78vh) wide and min(100vh, 56.25vw) tall (dvh where supported); the svg fills it. Nothing scrolls.

bands.header: 0 to 80. One line: the tool name, a measured dot, the phase concept; Hint, sound and restart as round controls far right.
bands.canvas: 92 to 640. One rounded card holding the key at its top right (Answer, Close, Enter, Next, or the Yes / No keys; no question bar), the working area (the whole card until Answer is tapped) and the answer drawer that slides in from the right; the summary page covers it at the end.
bands.footer: 652 to 900. The mascot at the far left on its ground line, the speech bubble beside it (y 656 to 892, the question and every line, printed), one small dot per phase at the right.

zones.layout: board, key only: no question bar, only its key at the right end of the top row (the question is on the bubble); the working area is the whole card (64, 108, 1472 x 520) until the child taps Answer, when the answer drawer (as tall as the working area, the key on its top row reading Close) slides in from the right
zones.controls: circles r 28 at cx 1388, 1460, 1532, cy 40: Hint (data-control again), sound, restart; 72-unit finger boxes
zones.dots: one small dot per phase at the footer's right (72-unit finger boxes, centred on the bubble), no text; in user AND AI mode each is a button (data-control phase-dot, data-phase k) that starts its phase

stage.noSidebar: There is no sidebar. The canvas takes every unit the chrome can spare.
stage.noScoreBox: There is no score box on the stage. The score leaves on finished and onComplete and is shown once, as stars on the summary page.

writeup.why: Write one real measure in two units, in its smallest unit and as a decimal in the larger unit, put a group's measures in order in one unit, add a group's weights, and measure the water a group drinks with a measuring jug.
writeup.look: A class record chart with a row for each child, record cards that flip through three forms, and a measuring jug marked in millilitres.
writeup.stage: Three bands across 1600 by 900. The header runs 0 to 80 and is one line only: 'Three Ways Recorder' in ink at the far left, a small dot set clear of the name, the phase title beside the dot on the same line, the host's navigation, and sound and restart as three round controls at the far right. The canvas runs 92 to 746, one rounded card on the paper colour. At its top left, at x 64, y 108 and 330 by 76, sits the running count: the number of measures recorded. It is never a score. The working area is 1086 by 528 at x 64, y 202. The class record chart fills the left of the area from x 90 to x 760: five rows, one for each child of the group, each 72 tall from y 250, under a header row at y 210 with columns for a long jump, a school bag's weight and a drink of water, and a total row at y 620. The record card stands at x 800, y 230, 300 by 110, with the measure in deep blue, labelled Given, and the Flip button under it at x 800, y 360. Each flip shows the card's next form in green, labelled Same measure, with a violet Unit fact beside it and a grey zero, labelled Place holder, wherever a place is held open. A row being dragged is amber. On the third phase the total row fills in green, labelled Answer. On the fourth phase the measuring jug stands at x 820, y 420, 160 wide and 260 tall, its marks and numbers in near-black ink, and each drink poured from it is read off its marks and entered in the water column. Down the right of the canvas, in the same rectangle on every phase and never animated in or out, the question sits above the answer slot at x 1186, y 250 (356 by 92) that holds what the child has given, and under it the pad at x 1170, y 368 (388 by 363). The pad is ten number keys with a point key, a delete key, and a key for each unit in use. The footer runs 758 to 900: the voice caption at the far left with its speaking dot beside it, measuring its own wrap and dropping a type size rather than spilling, and the phase bar at the right with the question count under it. There is no sidebar and no score box anywhere, and nothing is ever written over the working area. Content colours are the chapter's own, and the nine tools of this chapter share them. The measure the question gives, in the unit it is given in, is deep blue, labelled Given or Measure. The measure the working reaches, and a reading on a scale, is green, labelled Answer, Reading or Same measure. The places moved across the unit chart, and the worth of one small mark on a scale, are vermilion, labelled Move or One mark. A unit fact, the unit names on the chart and the other temperature scale are violet, labelled Unit fact, Unit or Other scale. The part taken away, and a part left over after sharing, are rose, labelled Taken away or Left over. The unit, column, mark or step being worked on now is amber. Grey is kept for a zero holding a place open inside a number, labelled Place holder, and for nothing else. Rulers, tapes, jugs, scales, thermometer tubes, chart lines, arrows, operation signs and step labels are near-black ink, and anything dimmed fades to half strength. Chrome never borrows one of the content colours, and each reading survives with the colour taken away, because a part is told by its written label before it is told by its colour.
writeup.finish: The group's chart stays up, every row in order, every card showing all three forms, and the totals in green.

phases.win: the three forms stand side by side, all green, all one jump
phases.does: flips the card and types each form in turn
phases.goal: one measure can be written in two units, in its smallest unit and as a decimal in the larger unit
phases.says: Flip it. Say the same jump another way.
phases.check: Away from the screen: say your own height in metres and centimetres, then in centimetres.
phases.feels: three different-looking forms standing side by side, all green, all one jump
phases.hands: Measure a jump on the playground with a tape, write it in metres and centimetres, then in centimetres, then as a decimal in metres, on three sides of one folded card.
phases.tries: First rung: write only the smallest-unit form. Second rung: write it as a decimal in metres. Third rung: the same task on a jump with no empty place, before the question's own jump returns.

writeup.delight: On the fourth phase, as the last drink is entered, the water column of the chart fills like a glass from the bottom up, and the total lands at the top in litres and millilitres.
writeup.opening: Every mount comes up already furnished for its phase with nothing yet recorded. On the first phase a long jump sits on a record card in metres and centimetres with the Flip button beside it. On the second four jumps sit on the chart, each written in a different form. On the third three weights sit on the chart in kilograms and grams above an empty total row. On the fourth a measuring jug marked in millilitres stands beside the water column of the chart. One thing moves, once: the Flip button, the first row, or the jug gives one slow pulse while the voice speaks its opening line.
writeup.freePlay: Any measures the group takes, entered on cards, flipped through three forms, ordered and added. Nothing to get right, no target and no timer. The child is left with the same stage and every control unlocked.
writeup.practice: Eight items over the four phases, easy first, on writing a measure three ways, ordering, adding weights and measuring water.
voiceLines: A class record chart, with a card to fill in.
Flip it. Say the same jump another way.
One unit first. Then shortest to longest.
All in grams. Add them. How many kilograms is that?
Pour it and read the jug. Now add them all.
A new measure for the chart. Record it the same way.
Free play. Record any measure and flip it through its forms.
Flip the card through all three forms. Do they all say the same measure?
You wrote real measures three ways, put them in order and added them.

observations.why: a measure can be written in two units, in its smallest unit, or as a decimal in the larger unit.
observations.soWhat: choose the form that suits the job: one unit to compare, the smallest unit to add.
observations.observe: The three forms on the card looked different but were all one jump.

observations.why: measures in one unit can be compared by their numbers alone.
observations.soWhat: put every measure in one unit, then order them.
observations.observe: The rows only fell into a clear order once every jump was in centimetres.

observations.why: adding whole numbers in the smallest unit needs no carrying across units.
observations.soWhat: add in the smallest unit, then write the total back in the larger unit.
observations.observe: The weights added in grams gave a total that bundled back into kilograms and grams.

observations.why: the jug is marked in millilitres.
observations.soWhat: a measuring jug turns a drink of water into a measure that can be added.
observations.observe: Each drink read off the jug's marks was a real measure, not a guess.

phases.screen: a long jump entered on a record card in metres and centimetres
phases.win: the three forms stand side by side, all green, all one jump
phases.traceback: a place chart under the cards puts the whole metres, the tenths and the hundredths in their places (a grey zero holding an empty place), and the card ends on the whole right form
ladder: How many centimetres make 1 m?
How many grams make 1 kg?
Is 60 cm more or less than half a metre?
7 cm is 7 hundredths of a metre.
The tenths place is empty, so a zero must hold it.

phases.screen: four jumps on the chart, each written in a different form
phases.win: the rows settle in order, and the jumps rise like steps
phases.traceback: every row's measure is shown in the chart's one unit beside it, the rows out of step are lit amber, and the right order is written under the chart
ladder: Compare the jumps in centimetres, not by their first number.
Can you compare 2.5 m with 208 cm as they are?
Write every bag's weight in grams before you order them.
208 cm is less than 2 m 15 cm, which is 215 cm.
In centimetres they are 215, 250, 208 and 251: order those.

phases.screen: three weights on the chart in kilograms and grams, and an empty total row
phases.win: the total turns green, in grams, in kilograms and grams, and as a decimal
phases.traceback: every bag is shown in grams, the grams column is added into the total row, and the total card ends on the whole right answer beside the unit fact
ladder: Add the grams of the three fruits.
Add the grams of the two bags.
What is each parcel's weight in grams?
Add the thousands again.
Take 1,000 g out of the total for each kilogram.

phases.screen: a measuring jug marked in millilitres beside the water column of the chart
phases.win: the water column fills, and the total turns green in litres and millilitres
phases.traceback: the drinks column is lit, its total is written in millilitres, the thousand millilitres are bundled into one litre, and the total card ends on the whole right answer
ladder: Add the millilitres of all five drinks.
Look at the lines on the side of the jug.
Add the four cups in millilitres first.
1,000 mL make 1 L.
Take 1,000 mL out of the total as one litre.
1 kg is 1,000 g, so start from 1,000.
Add the 250 g to the 1,000 g.
Every 10 cm is one tenth of a metre.
Count how many tenths of a metre 60 cm makes.
A first digit of 2 can mean 2 m or 208 cm.
How did the chart change once every card was flipped?
1 kg 80 g is 1,080 g, not 1,800 g.
In grams they are 1,080 g, 1,800 g and 1,008 g: order those.
Line the grams up by place, then add again.
Add 2,450 g and 1,675 g.
Add the three weights in grams again, place by place.
Write the grams total as kilograms: 1,000 g make 1 kg.
A guess can change from one child to the next.
Which choice lets two children get the same number?
325 + 410 + 195 + 290 gives the total in mL.
Every 1,000 mL of the total is 1 L.

onWrong.marks: Nothing is marked, nothing resets, no colour means good or bad. The child's answer stays; the pad re-opens after the traceback.
tracebacks: Phase 1: a place chart under the cards puts the whole metres, the tenths and the hundredths in their places (a grey zero holding an empty place), and the card ends on the whole right form
Phase 2: every row's measure is shown in the chart's one unit beside it, the rows out of step are lit amber, and the right order is written under the chart
Phase 3: every bag is shown in grams, the grams column is added into the total row, and the total card ends on the whole right answer beside the unit fact
Phase 4: the drinks column is lit, its total is written in millilitres, the thousand millilitres are bundled into one litre, and the total card ends on the whole right answer

voice.opening: A class record chart, with a card to fill in.
voice.onFreePlay: Free play. Flip a card through its three forms.
voice.onMiss: the item's own miss line, then the phase's two ladder rungs, shown at once UNDER the pinned instruction and kept until the child acts again
voice.onFinish: You wrote real measures three ways, put them in order and added them.
voice.rules: Silent: nothing is spoken (no device speech, no recorded clips, no Tap to start cover). The speech bubble is the guide: every instruction and hint is one printed page, numbers as words. The lesson is action-driven in every mode: a guide step's instruction stays until the child does the act it names; a wrong act shows that step's hint under the pinned instruction, a wrong answer the next rung of its ladder, and the hint stays unchanged until the child acts again; a right answer's next question, a phase's next phase and the summary's rows follow by themselves after a short celebration. The header's Hint key shows the step's hint or the next rung on demand. What is heard is sound effects (Web Audio), switched by the sound button, on in every mode. In classroom mode nothing waits for a tap except the pieces of a long line (the blinking arrow; a tap, Enter, Space, ArrowRight or PageDown on the bubble shows the next piece), and a tap on the bubble when nothing waits is the teacher's skip.

guide.playsOn: guide steps on phase 1, 2, 3, 4: the phase opens on its first instruction and waits for the child's act (getState guideStep, guideSteps, guideOn); the agent's check() performs the current step; the last act opens the first question. Other phases open on their printed teach lines, and a demo phase waits for the child's own act.

palette.rule: A content colour fills countable things only and chrome never borrows one; coloured numerals and words take a deeper ink of their colour (4.5:1).

toolQuestions.source: props.questions ?? props.additionalProps?.questions is read; the authored rows below keep their stage (fitHost returns null).

items.planQuestion: A long jump measures 3 m 7 cm. Write it in centimetres, and as a decimal in metres.

question.en: Now write a jump of 3 m 7 cm as a decimal in metres on the Decimal card.

items.planQuestion: A packet's label says 1 kg 250 g. Write the weight in grams.

question.en: A packet's label says 1 kg 250 g; write that weight in grams on the next card.

items.planQuestion: Write 4 m 60 cm as a decimal in metres.

question.en: Write 4 m 60 cm as a decimal in metres.

items.planQuestion: Four jumps measure 2 m 15 cm, 2.5 m, 208 cm and 2 m 51 cm. Put them in ascending order.

question.en: Flip the cards, then drag the rows from the shortest jump to the longest.

items.planQuestion: Before putting the jumps of a group in order, what must you do first?

question.en: Before you put jumps in order, what must you do first?

items.planAnswer: Write all of them in one unit

items.planQuestion: Put in ascending order: 1 kg 80 g, 1 kg 800 g, 1008 g.

question.en: Put the bags in order from the lightest to the heaviest.

items.planQuestion: Three bags of fruit weigh 1 kg 640 g, 2 kg 85 g and 1 kg 900 g. What do they weigh together?

question.en: Flip the cards, then add the three bags in kilograms and grams.

items.planQuestion: Two bags weigh 2 kg 450 g and 1 kg 675 g. What do they weigh together, in grams?

question.en: How many grams do the two bags weigh in all?

items.planQuestion: Three parcels weigh 850 g, 1 kg 20 g and 1.3 kg. What is their total, as a decimal in kilograms?

question.en: Write the three parcels' total as a decimal in kilograms on the total card.

items.planQuestion: Five children drink 210 mL, 235 mL, 190 mL, 260 mL and 255 mL of water, each poured from a measuring jug. How much is that in litres and millilitres?

question.en: Pour and read each drink, then write what the five drank in L and mL.

items.planQuestion: Why is a measuring jug used for the water each child drinks?

question.en: Why is each drink poured into a measuring jug first?

items.planAnswer: It is marked in millilitres, so each drink can be read, not guessed

items.planQuestion: Four cups hold 325 mL, 410 mL, 195 mL and 290 mL. How much is that altogether, in litres and millilitres?

question.en: Measure each cup in the jug, then total them in litres and millilitres.

ask.en: Four cups in L and mL?

scoring.wrong: costs nothing, never marked, counted only for first try accuracy
scoring.stars: one for finishing, two at sixty per cent right first time, three at ninety; hidden with the first-try line by showScore false
scoring.phaseMount: a mount scores every phase it plays, from its phase to the last (+5 a question; phases of 3, 3, 3, 3 questions)
scoring.finishCard: stars and the Right first time line under the phase rows on the summary page

hostContract.phase: absent (not a finite number): the whole lesson, phases one to 4 in a row, the summary page at the end, finished once. Present: rounded and clamped to one to 4; the tool starts at that phase and, as the NCERT tools do, walks on by itself after each phase's last question (its closing line, then 1.4 s), in user and AI mode alike, through phase 4 to the summary page (a tool with nextKey, runtime r48+: in user mode it waits for the child's blinking Next key instead, after every question and every phase, and the last phase's key opens the summary; AI mode, and a host that mounts one phase without navigableDots, walk on by themselves); finished once, from the summary page.
hostContract.navigableDots: true (or no phase): user mode, the phase dots are controls; otherwise AI mode, the dots show progress and the agent drives window.toolApi.

onProgress.done: questions right so far in this phase

hostContract.emits: every event is dispatched on window and, when framed, posted to window.parent as { type: 'event', name, detail }

getState: toolId, mediaId, mode, mountPhase, phase, phases, conceptId, objectiveIds, step, steps, item, items, stage (teach, demo, ask, win, idle, summary, free), question, questionText, choices, typed, keypadOpen, tries, answered, firstTry, score, maxScore, answerShown (only after the answer), complete, questionCount, muted (the sound effects), speaking (always false: the lesson is silent), voice ("silent"), mascot, summaryRow, played, classroom, held (a classroom's parked piece of a long line), instruction (the pinned line), hint (the hint under it, or null), guideStep / guideSteps / guideOn (a guide-steps phase only), phase, form, rows, r, r, order, jug, read, complete

terminalEvent.name: finished
terminalEvent.fires: once per mount, from the summary page after the last phase, 5 s after the page opens (its lines may still be going on); one-shot guarded and re-armed by restart or Play again; never sent at the end of an earlier phase (the tool walks on), and never if Free play or Play again is tapped first

sounds: Web Audio, no files, on in every mode (the sound button switches them): correct, wrong (soft), win at a phase end, cheer at the last, a tick when a piece snaps, and cut, settle and trade where the picture moves
